acar2025.title: Sustainable Nickel Extraction from Low-Grade Ores via Trametes versicolor: A Bioleaching Case Study on Olivine and Serpentine
acar2025.inspection: Read complete publisher PDF, all 14 original pages visually inspected, Figures1–8, Tables1–3, equations1–11 and graphical abstract. Publisher HTML independently retained. No supplementary material link found in inspected PDF/HTML; no claim of universal supplement absence.
acar2025.material: Two final chromite ore enrichment tailings supplied by Eti Krom, labelled olivine and serpentine, each a mixed assemblage; not pure minerals or the prior Odisha feed.
acar2025.organism: Source-labelled living Trametes versicolor OG2; fresh NCBI5325 species mapping. ITS/GenBank assignment mentioned but accession value not printed; no independently authenticated strain.
claims_and_limits: Culture-associated Ni/Fe/Mg/Si release with no reported abiotic leaching controls; Table3 control is a separate plate-growth assay.
No replicate count, error bars or uncertainty stated for leaching; no final-pH trajectory.
20g feed/L explicit loading; 2% by weight wording preserved; preparation has80mL nutrient aliquot diluted to1L, so aliquot concentrations are not final-medium claims.
150rpm versus200rpm methods conflict; approximately10^7 spore density has no unit.

Equation1 divides solution ppm by solid ppm without a mass-volume normalization. Figures5/7 values41.82/30.97 are retained only as author-labelled indices, not verified feed-mass extraction or recovered-product yield.
Figure4 oxalic acid9.562mg/L, reported after100-fold dilution but back-correction unclear; citrate and laccase mechanisms not measured here.
Cr(VI)-toxicity explanation unmeasured in leaching arm; chromite phase abundance does not identify Cr(VI).
SEM unavailable; Ni host substitution, organic complexes, redox routes and downstream recovery remain proposed. Industrial supplier does not demonstrate industrial bioprocess.
